comparables.name: Hugging Face (Hub + Inference Endpoints)
comparables.model: OSS libraries (Transformers, Tokenizers) free; Hub free for public repos. Revenue = PRO subscription ($9/mo/user), Team/Enterprise Hub seat-based ($20-50+/seat/mo), and managed Inference Endpoints billed per-minute at instance rate ($0.033/CPU-core-hr up to $80/hr for 8x H100), independent of request volume.
comparables.pricing: Free OSS + $9/mo PRO + $20-50+/seat/mo Enterprise + per-minute managed compute
comparables.lesson: The closest structural analog. HF gives away the tokenizer library and monetizes (a) governance/collaboration via per-seat Enterprise and (b) managed compute. For GeomTok, the tokenizer SDK should be free/Apache-2.0 to win adoption; money comes from a hosted endpoint + an Enterprise tier (SSO, SLA, private deploy, support). Critically, HF's Inference Endpoints bill for provisioned compute-time, NOT per-call — the right framing when the unit cost is just CPU seconds.

comparables.name: Replicate (Cog OSS + managed inference)
comparables.model: Cog (model-packaging tool) is open source and free; the managed run-API is billed per-second of compute by hardware tier. Public models bill only active processing time (setup/idle free); private models bill all online time. Acquired into Cloudflare.
comparables.pricing: Per-second compute: $0.000025/s CPU up to $0.001525/s H100; no idle cost on public models
comparables.lesson: Per-second-of-actual-compute pricing is the honest model when value tracks runtime. But for a deterministic tokenizer, a CPU call is sub-millisecond — per-second billing would round to fractions of a cent and feel absurd to meter. Take the lesson (give away the packaging/OSS tool, charge for managed runtime) but aggregate the billing unit up to per-1K-icons or per-1M-tokens so invoices are legible.

comparables.name: Modal (serverless compute infra)
comparables.model: Proprietary platform; granular per-second metering of CPU ($0.0000394/core/s), GPU, and memory ($0.0000067/GiB/s), plus a flat Team plan ($250/mo) and $30/mo free credits. No OSS core.
comparables.pricing: Granular per-second CPU/GPU/memory metering + $250/mo Team plan + free credits
comparables.lesson: Shows the platform-fee + metered-usage pattern: a flat monthly floor ($250) on top of consumption smooths revenue and signals seriousness. For GeomTok, a modest platform fee per paid tier (covering SLA/support) plus usage overages is more defensible than pure pay-go, because the marginal CPU cost of tokenization is near-zero and pure metering can't sustain margin.

comparables.name: Unstructured.io (OSS library + managed parsing API)
comparables.model: Open-source `unstructured` ETL library is free and drives adoption; managed Serverless API is pay-as-you-go per page ($1 per 1,000 pages = $0.001/page) with 15,000 free pages, no minimums. Enterprise = VPC/dedicated, data isolation, support, custom pricing. Claims 50x speed vs OSS lib.
comparables.pricing: $0.001/page (per 1,000 pages); 15K free pages; Enterprise VPC custom
comparables.lesson: The single best template for GeomTok. Same shape: cheap deterministic document-processing on CPU, OSS core for trust/adoption, managed API priced per discrete artifact (a page). GeomTok's 'page' is an icon/SVG. Per-artifact pricing (~per 1,000 SVGs) is intuitive for buyers and decouples price from raw CPU cost. The OSS lib being slower than the managed service (their stated 50x) is the wedge that converts free users to paid — GeomTok can mirror this with batching, caching, and hosted vocab management.

comparables.name: Pinecone (managed vector DB)
comparables.model: Fully proprietary/closed-source (no community edition), pure managed SaaS. Serverless usage metered on read units ($8.25-24/M), write units ($2/M), storage ($0.33/GB/mo), with a $50/mo Standard minimum and $500/mo Enterprise minimum.
comparables.pricing: Usage units (reads/writes/storage) + $50/mo Standard min, $500/mo Enterprise min
comparables.lesson: The counter-example on openness: Pinecone proves you CAN win a category closed-source, but it's now flanked by OSS rivals (Weaviate/Qdrant/Milvus) precisely because devs distrust lock-in for core infra. Since GeomTok is committed to Apache-2.0, this validates the OSS-core moat against future closed copycats. Borrow the monthly-minimum mechanic ($50/$500 floors) — it filters tire-kickers and guarantees revenue per active account despite cheap unit costs.

comparables.name: Resend (OSS react-email + email API)
comparables.model: react-email is free OSS with 2M weekly npm downloads (top-of-funnel). Managed API: Free (3,000 emails/mo), Pro $20-35/mo (50K-100K emails, slider), Scale with declining per-email rates ($0.90 down to $0.46 per 1,000), Enterprise sales-led with SLAs/MSAs.
comparables.pricing: Free 3K/mo; Pro $20-35/mo volume slider; Scale per-1K declining; Enterprise custom
comparables.lesson: Masterclass in OSS-as-distribution: a beloved free library (react-email) feeds the paid sending API. For GeomTok, the open tokenizer + GeomTok-Eval are the react-email equivalent — they should be genuinely best-in-class to seed every SVG/icon pipeline. The volume-slider Pro tier ($20-35) and declining per-1K rates at scale are exactly the legible, self-serve packaging GeomTok needs for the cheap-CPU reality.

comparables.name: Deepgram (speech-to-text API)
comparables.model: Per-minute usage pricing (~$0.07-0.08/min PAYG, lower on Growth), with self-hosted/on-prem deployment offered as an Enterprise lever (Docker/K8s). Free credits, Growth (discounted), Enterprise (custom models, volume discounts, self-host).
comparables.pricing: Per-minute (~$0.0075-0.08/min) + Growth discount tier + Enterprise self-host/custom
comparables.lesson: Best analog for the deployment-flexibility lever. Deterministic-ish processing priced per natural unit (minute of audio), with the big-ticket monetization being Enterprise self-hosted/on-prem for customers with data-residency needs. GeomTok's design-tool/SaaS buyers (Figma/Canva-like) will often want on-prem or VPC tokenization for IP reasons — package that as the premium Enterprise SKU, since the OSS license technically lets them self-host for free, so the paid value must be support, SLA, managed vocab, and updates.

comparables.name: Recraft (AI vector/SVG generation)
comparables.model: Credit-based consumer/prosumer SaaS for AI SVG generation: Free 50 daily credits, paid $10-55/mo by credit bundle and seats; API ~$0.08 per generated image. Not OSS — a downstream application, not infra.
comparables.lesson: Defines the adjacent demand and the 'do NOT compete here' line. Recraft is a vertically-integrated GENERATION app charging $0.08/SVG to end-creatives — that price reflects model inference + brand value, not tokenization. GeomTok should sit UNDER tools like Recraft as the tokenization/eval layer they'd otherwise build in-house. It confirms there's real money in vector-AI, and validates GeomTok's honest stance: sell the production-ready tokenizer+eval now, treat generation as a later phase rather than fighting Recraft head-on.

pricing_recommendation:
Adopt a four-tier OSS-core + managed model, closely mirroring Unstructured.io and Resend, with the billing unit aggregated up from raw CPU cost so invoices stay legible.

1) OPEN SOURCE (Apache-2.0, free forever): the GeomTok tokenizer SDK, the scalar fixed-point codec, FSA grammar-constrained decoder, and GeomTok-Eval. This is distribution, not a product — it must be best-in-class to seed every SVG/icon pipeline (the react-email/Cog/unstructured-library role). Self-hosting is fully permitted; that is intentional top-of-funnel.

2) MANAGED API — usage-priced per ARTIFACT, not per CPU-second. Because tokenization is sub-millisecond CPU work, never meter per-second (it rounds to nothing) and never copy LLM per-token inference pricing (off by orders of magnitude). Price per 1,000 SVGs/icons tokenized — the exact mechanic Unstructured uses per 1,000 pages. Concrete starting point: Free 25,000 icons/mo (adoption); then a usage rate in the ~$0.50-$2.00 per 1,000 icons range (i.e. $0.0005-$0.002 per icon) with declining rates at volume, à la Resend's $0.90→$0.46 per 1,000. The margin here is for managed vocabulary versioning, batching, caching, round-trip/SSIM validation, and uptime — NOT for the CPU cycles. Add round-trip verification and a hosted GeomTok-Eval run as billable add-ons (eval is the unique, game-resistant asset with no public equivalent).

3) PLATFORM FLOORS to defend margin on cheap compute. Borrow Pinecone/Modal: a monthly minimum (~$50/mo Standard, scaling to ~$500/mo for higher tiers) on paid plans. This guarantees revenue per active account and filters tire-kickers, which pure pay-go on near-zero-marginal-cost compute cannot do.

4) ENTERPRISE / SELF-HOSTED (sales-led, the real revenue). Since Apache-2.0 lets anyone self-host, Enterprise value is NOT the bits — it's: SLA + support/consulting, on-prem/VPC deployment for IP/data-residency (the Deepgram self-host lever, which design-tool vendors will demand for proprietary asset libraries), managed vocab training on the customer's icon corpus, SSO/governance (HF Enterprise Hub seat model), and integration/consulting engagements. Price as annual contracts with a platform fee + usage, typically $25K-$150K+ ACV depending on volume and deployment.

GENERATION (toy-scale today, 2.5M params/CPU/monochrome): do NOT price or promise it now. Position it as roadmap; gate a future generation API behind real large-data training investment, and if/when shipped, price it on the Replicate/Modal per-second-of-GPU model since its cost structure is genuinely inference-like — completely separate from the tokenizer's cheap-CPU economics.

Net: the tokenizer+eval monetize via (free OSS → per-1K-icon managed API with monthly floors → Enterprise self-host/support contracts). Honesty caveat: exact per-1K price points should be calibrated against design-vendor willingness-to-pay in early pilots — the $0.50-$2.00/1K range is anchored on Unstructured's $1/1K pages, not on observed GeomTok demand, and may need adjustment.
positioning: GeomTok is the open-source, geometry-native tokenization and evaluation layer for vector AI — the reliable foundation that design-tool and SaaS vendors build on instead of inventing SVG tokenization themselves. Where text tokenizers produce 0% renderable SVG, GeomTok's geometric primitive tokens are a verified, production-grade substrate (100% parse and round-trip on 2,682 real-world icons, 1.78px mean coordinate fidelity, 0.929 render SSIM, and 3.54x compression versus a domain-trained text tokenizer at matched vocabulary), and they're proven the BEST downstream modeling substrate (576 vs 775 bits/icon, ~28 sigma) — because, as our research shows, compression is not modelability. We pair this with GeomTok-Eval, the only render-based, game-resistant protocol for measuring tokenizer quality, with no public equivalent. The tokenizer and evaluator are Apache-2.0 and free to self-host; we make money running them as a managed API and as enterprise/on-prem deployments with SLAs, managed vocabularies, and support. We are infrastructure that sits beneath generation products like Recraft, not a competitor to them — and we are honest that high-quality SVG generation is a later, large-data phase, while the tokenizer and eval are ready for production today.
market_size_notes:
Demand is real and growing fast, but GeomTok's serviceable market is a thin infrastructure slice beneath these headline numbers — sizing should be bottom-up by design-vendor count, not top-down off these TAMs.

Headline markets (third-party analyst estimates; treat as directional, vendors' methodologies vary widely):
- AI in design: ~$20.1B (2025) → ~$60.7B (2030), ~25% CAGR (Knowledge Sourcing).
- AI-powered design tools: ~$6.7B (2025) → ~$18.2B (2030), ~22% CAGR (The Business Research Company / Research and Markets).
- Generative AI in design (narrower): ~$1.0B (2025) → ~$16.9B (2035), ~33% CAGR (Precedence Research).
- Generative design (engineering/CAD-leaning): ~$3.6B (2025) → ~$11.9B (2033), ~16% CAGR (Straits).

Reality check for GeomTok: these figures count end-user design APPLICATIONS and creative spend, not tokenization infrastructure. GeomTok's actual addressable wedge is the much smaller set of organizations that build vector/SVG ML pipelines: design-tool/SaaS vendors (Figma/Canva-class platforms, icon libraries like the Noun Project/Iconscout, no-code/website builders), plus AI/ML teams training SVG models. That is realistically on the order of low-thousands of companies worldwide, of which only the subset doing serious vector-AI is a buyer today. A credible bottom-up SAM is better modeled as (number of design/vector-AI vendors that would adopt) x (blended ACV of roughly $25K-$150K Enterprise + self-serve usage) — likely a low-tens-of-millions early addressable market that grows with the generative-design wave, not a billion-dollar TAM. The strategic bet is that as vector AI matures (Recraft, Adobe Firefly vectors, Canva), every serious player needs reliable tokenization + objective evaluation, and GeomTok aims to be the default standard for that layer — analogous to how Hugging Face Tokenizers became default for text. Uncertainty is high: there is no published market figure for 'SVG/vector tokenization infrastructure' specifically, so any number is an extrapolation and should be validated through design-vendor discovery calls before being used in fundraising or planning."
